bib.title: Overcoming catastrophic forgetting in neural networks

question: Can a neural network learn tasks sequentially without catastrophically forgetting earlier ones, without storing old data or adding capacity?
hypothesis: Slowing learning on weights that are important to old tasks (task-specific synaptic consolidation) lets one fixed-capacity network keep old tasks while learning new ones.
contributions: Elastic weight consolidation (EWC): a quadratic penalty weighted by the diagonal Fisher information anchoring parameters to old-task values
Demonstration on permuted MNIST sequences and on ten Atari games learned sequentially with a DQN agent
Fisher-overlap analysis showing layers closer to the output are shared across tasks
Perturbation test showing the diagonal Fisher is a useful but over-confident importance estimate

method.summary: EWC adds a penalty sum_i lambda/2 F_i (theta_i - theta*_A,i)^2 to the new-task loss, with F the diagonal Fisher information at the old-task solution (Laplace approximation of the task-A posterior). Tested on permuted-MNIST fully connected nets and on a DQN with HMM-based task recognition over ten Atari games.
method.task: continual learning (permuted MNIST classification; sequential Atari reinforcement learning)

datasets.name: Permuted MNIST
datasets.split: validation set used for early stopping; test sets used for curves
datasets.source: MNIST (LeCun et al., 1998); each task a fixed random pixel permutation
datasets.preprocessing: fixed random permutation of input pixels per task

datasets.name: Atari 2600 games
datasets.size: 10 games per experiment drawn from a pool of 19; 10 sets of 10 games
datasets.preprocessing: 210x160 frames downsampled to 84x84 bilinear, YUV grayscale channel, 4 latest frames stacked; rewards clipped to 1; action repeat 4; up to 30 no-ops; full 18-action set

models.name: DQN with EWC and task recognition (Atari)
models.params: inferred: about four times the standard DQN network
models.architecture: conv 8x8 stride 4 32 filters; conv 4x4 stride 2 64 filters; conv 3x3 stride 1 128 filters; FC 1024; per-game biases and gains per layer; 18 outputs

training.objective: MNIST: task-B loss + EWC quadratic penalty (Eq 3). Atari: Double Q-learning (van Hasselt 2016) + EWC penalty with Fisher recomputed at each task switch
training.optimizer: MNIST: SGD (optimizer variant not stated). Atari: RMSProp, momentum 0, decay 0.95
training.lr: MNIST: 1e-3 (Fig 2A, 3C), 1e-5 to 1e-3 searched (Fig 2B). Atari: 2.5e-4, max learning rate 2.5e-3
training.batch_size: Atari: 32 experiences every 4 steps; MNIST: small batches, size not stated
training.steps: Atari: EWC penalty only after 20 million frames in a game; total steps not stated
training.dropout: MNIST SGD+dropout baseline: 0.2 on input, 0.5 on hidden layers; none for EWC runs in Fig 2A
training.regularisation: EWC lambda: Atari 400 (Fisher multiplier); MNIST lambda not stated. Early stopping for the dropout baseline (stop after validation error rises for more than five steps, reset to best weights)
training.seeds: Atari: 4 random seeds for each of 10 sets of 10 games; MNIST not stated

other.fisher_estimate: 100 minibatches drawn from the replay buffer per task
other.epsilon: 1 for 5e4 steps then linear to 0.01 over next 1e6 (text) / 1050000 end (Table 2)
other.task_recognition: HMM over task context, factored Dirichlet-multinomial pixel models on 42x42 downscaled images, window W=4, update every 4 steps, switch rate alpha=1/t
other.mnist_random_search: 50 hyperparameter combinations per experiment; best reported

inference.samples: Fig 3C: ten full game episodes per perturbation level, new random weight perturbation every timestep

metrics.name: Total human-normalized score (Atari)
metrics.definition: sum over ten games of human-normalized score, each clipped to 1; 0 = random agent

metrics.name: Test accuracy/error per permuted-MNIST task
metrics.definition: performance on test set of each task during sequential training

metrics.name: Fisher overlap
metrics.definition: 1 - d^2 where d^2 is Frechet distance between unit-trace Fisher matrices

baselines: SGD with dropout and early stopping (Goodfellow et al. 2014)
eval.protocol: Atari scores averaged over 10 sets of 10 games and 4 seeds; MNIST results from best of 50 random hyperparameter combos; no significance tests reported

evidence.quote: The target network is updated every 3 × 104 time steps.

results.claim: With plain SGD the Atari agent never learns more than one game; total human-normalized score stays below one, while EWC lets it learn multiple games.
results.setup: DQN with task recognition, ten Atari games learned sequentially, plain SGD baseline
results.quote: the agent never learns to play more than one game and the harm inﬂicted by forgetting the old games means that the total human-normalized score remains below one
results.note: Exact EWC score is only shown in Fig 3B, not in text

results.claim: EWC with learned task labels is only modestly worse than giving the agent the true task labels.
results.note: Paper says 'The improvement here was only modest'; no number

results.claim: EWC on permuted MNIST keeps old-task accuracy while learning new tasks; L2 cannot learn task B; SGD forgets A (qualitative from Fig 2A, no numbers in text).
results.setup: Permuted MNIST, 2x400 ReLU net, lr 1e-3, 20 epochs per dataset

results.claim: Prior methods (dropout etc.) reached reasonable results only up to two random permutations; EWC handles many tasks with modest error growth.
results.source: Srivastava et al. 2013; Goodfellow et al. 2014
results.quote: they have only achieved reasonable results on up to two random permutations

results.claim: EWC does not reach the score of training ten separate DQNs.
results.quote: it does not reach the score that would have been obtained by training ten separate DQNs

results.claim: Perturbations shaped by the inverse Fisher hurt less than uniform ones, validating the diagonal Fisher as importance estimate; but perturbing the Fisher nullspace hurts as much, so uncertainty is under-estimated.
results.quote: it is therefore likely that the chief limitation of the current implementation is that it under-estimates parameter uncertainty

results.setup: Atari DQN, tuned by hyperparameter search
results.quote: a scaling factor for the EWC penalty of 400

results.claim: EWC run time is linear in parameters and training examples.
results.quote: EWC has a run time which is linear in both the number of parameters and the number of training examples

limits: Diagonal Fisher / Laplace point estimate under-estimates parameter uncertainty (authors' stated main weakness).
EWC on Atari falls short of ten separate single-game DQNs.
Main text gives almost no numeric results; scores only in figures.
Needs a task boundary (Fisher computed at each task switch) and one stored Fisher and anchor per task; storage per parameter grows.
Only small MLPs and a small DQN tested; no language or vision-language models, no pretrained-model fine-tuning.
Penalty only applied to games with at least 20 million frames experienced.

terms.definition: knowledge of previously learnt task(s) is abruptly lost as information relevant to the current task is incorporated
an algorithm that slows down learning on certain weights based on how important they are to previously seen tasks

figures.caption: EWC ensures task A is remembered whilst training on task B (schematic parameter space).
figures.why: Shows why per-weight stiffness beats uniform L2.

figures.caption: Results on the permuted MNIST task (A curves for EWC, L2, SGD; B average across tasks vs dropout; C Fisher overlap vs depth).
figures.why: Core evidence of forgetting and its prevention.

figures.caption: Results on Atari task (schedule, total scores, perturbation sensitivity).
figures.why: Shows RL result and the Fisher validity test.
